title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
summary: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea is an anonymous Greek-language sailing guide written by an Egyptian merchant around the middle of the first century CE. It leads from Egyptian Red Sea ports down the African coast and around Arabia to western and southern India, naming ports such as Myos Hormos, Berenice, Adulis, Barygaza and Muziris, with their goods and the monsoon months for sailing.

uncertainty.note: University of Washington: "around the middle of the first century CE"; World History Encyclopedia: written "sometime between 40-55 CE", and Schoff (1912) and others place it at 60 CE. The range 40 to 60 CE spans those figures. The id says 50.

importance.justification: The main surviving first-century description of the Indian Ocean trade routes between Roman Egypt, Arabia, East Africa and India.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the path: the Periplus names more stops (Muza, Cana, the Indus mouth) than I mapped; I kept only stops whose coordinates I could take from Wikidata, and I treated Wikidata's Bharuch as Barygaza and its Muziris point as the Periplus port, an identification neither opened page states. The date window is mine, built from the two pages; the id says 50.

beats.caption: The guide starts at the Egyptian Red Sea ports of Myos Hormos and Berenice and follows the African coast south to Adulis.
Ships from Arabia and from Barygaza trade across the sea, and the author notes the months to sail from Egypt with the monsoon.
The route continues to western and southern India, where Muziris and Nelcynda are described as of leading importance.
